INDIA'S FIRST TOKENIZED CORPORATE BONDS GO LIVE

-India just put more than ₹1,025 crore of ordinary corporate debt onto tokenized rails in one week.REC raised ₹500 crore at 7.30% on Sept 7. L&T followed with ₹500 crore at 7.40%, becoming the first private issuer. IIFL Finance added ₹25 crore at 9.10%, the first non-PSU NBFC deal.

-These are still regular rupee bonds. Credit risk, coupons, and legal claims have not moved onto a public chain. What changed is settlement: bidding stayed on NSE’s electronic platform, holdings were recorded on NSDL and CDSL Demat 2.0, and cash moved through wholesale CBDC wallets with same-day atomic delivery versus payment.

-The catch is the market around them. The notes are listed, but there is still no live secondary trading venue; retail access is closed, and only institutions with both a Demat 2.0 wallet and a wholesale e₹ wallet can participate. Exchanges have been expected to build a trading layer later this year.

-The bonds are live. The market is not.

It's that smart consumer companies now treat packaging as a strategic lever, not an afterthought. 

The ones building flexibility into their supply chain today are the ones festive season won't catch off guard.

That's how businesses actually get built to last.

Here's the sharpest bit. For beer, prices are capped by the state, unlike soft drinks.

So brewers can't simply pass on higher costs to consumers. 

They're absorbing it instead, while waiting out the storm.

Glass brings its own equation. It needs industrial gas to manufacture, and it's heavier and more fragile to transport.

So this isn't a free swap. 

It's a trade-off between packaging types, not a total escape from rising costs.

So beverage and alcohol companies did what any smart business does when one channel narrows.

They diversified. Faster shift to glass and PET bottles to keep shelves stocked for the festive rush.

On top of that, India tightened safety and quality norms for imported aluminium sheets this year.

Good for standards. But it also meant fewer suppliers could legally sell into India right now.

More friction, right as festive season demand was picking up.

Naturally, prices flew up. Nearly 25% higher than last year at one point.

India felt this hard. 

We're the world's second largest aluminium producer, but we don't make enough of the specific thin, food-grade sheet that beverage cans need.

We import most of it.

Making aluminium needs huge amounts of electricity and raw material shipped in by sea.

The crisis disrupted both for Gulf producers. Smelters shut down. Ships couldn't move through the Strait of Hormuz.

Nearly 9% of the world's aluminium supply took a hit, almost overnight.

So China capped how much aluminium it produces every year.

The world still had other suppliers to lean on. A shortage was expected, but a small, manageable one.

Then came the West Asia crisis.

It starts in China.

China makes nearly 60% of the world's aluminium. 

Late 2024, it pulled back a tax benefit that made its aluminium cheap for the rest of the world.

Why? China wants to use more of its own aluminium to build higher-value products, not just export raw metal.

Earlier this year, Diet Coke cans quietly vanished from stores in Indian metros.

Not the drink. Just the can.

The real story behind this has nothing to do with Coca-Cola. 

It starts on the other side of the world.

WHY KEEP AN EYE ON THE NIFTY SME EMERGE UNIVERSE?
The interesting part of the SME segment is that many businesses are still in the expansion phase - adding capacity, entering new markets, building customers and scaling their operations.

But this also means higher risk.
So, don't simply look at a stock because it is part of the Nifty SME Emerge universe or because its price has performed well.

For every company, we should study:
▪️ Business model & industry opportunity
▪️ Revenue and earnings growth
▪️ Balance sheet
▪️ Cash-flow generation
▪️ Debt & working capital
▪️ ROE / ROCE
▪️ Promoter holding & pledge
▪️ Order book and order inflow
▪️ Capacity & utilisation
▪️ Capex plans
▪️ Customer concentration
▪️ Annual reports
▪️ Quarterly results
▪️ Concalls / investor presentations
▪️ Corporate announcements
▪️ Management quality
▪️ Valuation
▪️ Technical structure & liquidity

The Nifty SME Emerge index itself has at least 20 constituents, with eligibility requiring NSE Emerge listing and a minimum trading frequency at quarterly review; constituents are weighted by free-float market capitalisation.

Also, SME stocks can have different liquidity and trading characteristics compared with mainboard companies. NSE's Emerge platform uses market-making mechanisms, and some SME securities can trade through call-auction arrangements depending on the security.

So the objective here is simple:
Don't chase the stock.
Study the business.
Track the execution.
Research the numbers.

Can an alternative asset manager turn lumpy private equity exits into predictable public-market earnings?

In its first quarterly call since listing, Gaja Alternative AMC reported total income of 51.8 crore rupees, up 26% year-on-year, while PAT grew 35% to 27.2 crore rupees. Operating leverage was visible, with expenses growing just 14% to 19.9 crore rupees, pulling the cost-to-income ratio down to 38.4%.

Yet beneath the headline beat lies the central tension of the asset management model. Performance income—comprising carried interest and mark-to-market sponsor gains—accounted for 29.7 crore rupees, or 57% of total revenue. Pure management fee income was 16.0 crore rupees, up just 7%.

When analysts pressed for visibility on carry realizations over the next 12 months, management held a firm line: zero forward earnings guidance as a matter of board policy.

Instead, management anchored the growth thesis to fund expansion. With SEBI approvals in hand, the firm is preparing to launch flagship Fund 5 targeting 2,500 crore rupees and Eastgate Secondaries targeting 1,500 crore rupees. If closed, this 4,000 crore rupee pipeline would more than double the current fee-paying committed capital of roughly 3,200 crore rupees.

Do the math on the fee base: 4,000 crore rupees of new committed capital at standard 1.5-2.0% annual management fees would add 60-80 crore rupees in recurring annual top line once fully mobilized. But until those first closes land, quarterly earnings will swing with public valuations and exit timing.

Fund 5 fundraising traction, the launch of the secondaries platform, and exit realizations across mature funds are the metrics to monitor.

That's the scoreboard to watch.

Why it matters: Overdependence on a few cloud and technology providers could create systemic vulnerabilities across the entire financial system, warns the RBI's top technology regulator.

A front-page report in Times of India says India's Financial Fraud Risk Indicator (FRI), launched by the department of telecommunications in May 2025, has helped banks and payment platforms prevent suspected fraudulent transactions worth Rs 5,043.7 crore in 15 months. The system assigns mobile numbers risk ratings and feeds alerts directly to banks and UPI platforms, enabling real-time interception of risky payments. Experts say the system has made fraud operations costlier, though fraudsters may try to evade it through fraudulent SIM cards or virtual numbers.
Why it matters: India's Financial Fraud Risk Indicator has proven its worth by blocking nearly Rs 5,100 crore in suspected fraudulent transactions, making fraud operations increasingly costlier for criminals.
Key detail: The system assigns mobile numbers risk ratings and feeds alerts directly to banks and UPI platforms, enabling real-time interception of risky payments over 15 months.

A front-page report in Business Standard says Larsen & Toubro and IIFL Finance entered India's tokenised bond market this week, raising Rs 500 crore and Rs 25 crore respectively. REC had earlier completed the first such issuance, raising Rs 750 crore through a 20-month bond. A front-page report in Free Press Journal says domestic credit growth in India could moderate to 15% by March 2027 from around 18% currently, according to Jefferies. Why it matters: Jefferies' forecast of credit growth slowing to 15 percent by March 2027 reflects a maturing credit cycle, with implications for bank profitability and lending strategies.

Why it matters: The launch of forex services through Bharat Connect marks a significant step toward democratising foreign exchange access for retail customers across multiple banking channels.

Next step: Customers should explore the expanded forex options for overseas remittances and forex card reloads with competitive live rates.

A front-page report in Indian Express says SEBI has proposed two broad changes to regulations for Market Infrastructure Institutions on 18 July 2026. The regulator wants to ease board restrictions and introduce standard qualifications for four key managerial positions including Chief Technology Officer, Chief Information Security Officer, Compliance Officer, and Chief Risk Officer. Why it matters: SEBI's proposed changes to Market Infrastructure Institution regulations aim to modernise governance standards while attracting qualified talent to critical financial market roles.

Why it matters: Paytm's strategic shift into AI agent sales represents a landmark business pivot, leveraging its technology capabilities to serve banks, insurers, and financial institutions in India and the UAE.

Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced the proposed Maharashtra Digitisation and Exchange of Land Token Asset Act at the Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai on Wednesday, with the framework being developed with inputs from SEBI, BSE, NSE, and experts from industry, technology, law, and academia. Land assets covered under the new framework are estimated to be worth fifty lakh crore rupees.

Why it matters: Tokenising land assets could transform India's real estate market by enhancing liquidity and enabling fractional ownership through blockchain technology.

Key detail: The framework is being developed with inputs from SEBI, BSE, NSE, and experts from industry, technology, law, and academia. Land assets covered are estimated to be worth fifty lakh crore rupees.

RBI Executive Director P. Vasudevan announced this during a fireside chat at the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai on September 9, noting that the central bank has already tested the platform with 248 certificate-of-deposit transactions worth Rs 17,000 crore.

Why it matters: Gold tokenisation on a CBDC-settled platform could reshape commodity trading and bring transparency to India's gold market.

Key detail: The RBI has already tested tokenisation with 248 certificate-of-deposit transactions worth Rs 17,000 crore.

Source: Deccan Chronicle, front-page report.

4. RBI Settles Tokenised Financial Instruments Using CBDC
A front-page report in Asian Age says the Reserve Bank of India settled tokenised financial instruments using central bank digital currency. The RBI tested tokenisation with 248 certificate-of-deposit transactions worth twenty-one thousand seven hundred crore rupees. RBI deputy governor Rohit Jain and Niti Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri highlighted challenges and economic priorities at the event.

Why it matters: CBDC-settled tokenisation bridges the gap between traditional finance and blockchain-based markets, reducing settlement risk and increasing efficiency.

Key detail: RBI deputy governor Rohit Jain and Niti Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri highlighted challenges and economic priorities at the event.

The Telangana State Road Transport Corporation is now planning to extend operations to a 24x7 service, with more night routes to be added soon. These offshore exchanges operated from various jurisdictions worldwide but actively solicited Indian users without ensuring compliance with Indian financial laws.

A front-page report in Times of India says Lakhanpal, who allegedly posed as a finance ministry official, was arrested in the UAE for defrauding investors of more than Rs 113 crore through a fake money trade coin cryptocurrency scheme in 2017-18. The Enforcement Directorate shared his whereabouts with Thane police, leading to his arrest on September 1, after which the government initiated extradition proceedings. Investigators also found a police officer in Thane handled his office and clients, and Lakhanpal had fled India after acquiring Antigua and Barbuda passports.

India’s New Industrial Revolution is already being rewarded.
Jefferies highlighted Space, Semiconductors & Electronics, Data Centers, Solar Manufacturing and Aerospace as the next big growth engines.
The stock market has taken notice — and in several cases is pricing the opportunity well ahead of the Nifty 50.
Here’s the clear scorecard:
Aerospace & Defence (incl. Space ecosystem)
The strongest performer.
Nifty India Defence has decisively beaten the Nifty 50 across 1-year and multi-year periods.
HAL, BEL, MTAR Technologies, Data Patterns, Astra Microwave, Sansera Engineering and Azad Engineering have delivered standout returns.
Global OEMs (Boeing & Airbus) are steadily increasing Indian sourcing. Pure space startups remain private — so listed suppliers are capturing the re-rating.
Data Centers
The AI infrastructure trade is very much alive in India.
Related names in optical fibre, power, cooling and transformers have added tens of billions in market value even as broader indices lagged.
Sterlite Technologies and HFCL turned multi-baggers on hyperscaler demand. Power-equipment and precision cooling plays (CG Power, Hitachi Energy, MTAR) are also clear beneficiaries.
Solar Manufacturing
India is already the world’s No. 2 solar PV manufacturer.
Capacity is scaling rapidly and localisation is heading toward ~90% of the value chain by 2030.
Premier Energies, Waaree Energies, Emmvee and peers have posted strong revenue and profit growth. Returns remain solid, though more selective after the earlier rally.
Semiconductors & Electronics
Still early-stage.
Policy has moved from intent to execution ($20 bn+ pipeline + fresh incentives). Gains are showing more in electronics manufacturing and component plays than pure semiconductor names so far.
Versus Nifty 50
While the benchmark has been range-bound or modest, these thematic pockets have delivered clear relative outperformance — classic behaviour when structural themes gain visibility.
Will the growth continue?
Yes — on a multi-year structural basis.
Policy support is broad (space sector opening, data-centre tax holidays, PLI schemes, localisation mandates). Domestic demand is rising. Global China+1, AI build-out and aerospace supply-chain shifts all favour India. Order books and capacity under construction give multi-year visibility.
Risks remain: elevated valuations, execution delays, and limited pure-play listed options in space and advanced semis. Volatility will stay high.

Har engine ke andar ek aisi cheez hoti hai jise koi nahi dekhta.

Engine bearing. Crankshaft aur connecting rod ke beech ki patli layer. Micron level ki precision. Ghiste rehna uska kaam hai, taaki engine na ghise.

Kolhapur ki Menon Bearings yahi banati hai — bearings, bushes, thrust washers. Saath mein aluminium die-casting (Alkop) aur braking components. Customers mein Maruti, Mahindra, Cummins, Kirloskar, Eicher. Exports UK, Spain, Israel aur USA tak.

Q1 FY27:

Revenue ₹91.79 crore, 36.57% up. Highest-ever quarter.
Consolidated PAT ₹14.11 crore, 67.38% up.
PBT ₹18.51 crore, 67.4% up.
₹2 per share interim dividend, saal ke beech mein.

Ab do cheezein jo headline ke neeche hain.

Pehli — margin.

Other income hataakar operating margin 21.92% rahi. Q4 FY26 mein 24.79% thi. Karib 287 basis point sequentially neeche.

Revenue record pe, margin peak se peeche. Company ne khud bataya ki production badhne se cost badhe.

Doosri — aur yeh zyada interesting hai.

Consolidated PAT ₹14.11 crore, standalone ₹11.23 crore. Farak ₹2.88 crore — subsidiary ka hissa.

Sequential dekhiye. Standalone Q4 ke ₹9.50 crore se ₹11.23 crore — 18% up. Par consolidated ₹13.78 crore se ₹14.11 crore — sirf 2.4%.

Matlab parent tez badhi, subsidiary sequentially gira. Ek hi result mein do alag directions.

Ab structural baat.

Engine bearing, bush, thrust washer — yeh sab engine ke parts hain. EV mein engine hi nahi hota. Yaani is company ka content per vehicle EV share badhne ke saath ghatega. Tyre ya glass ki tarah fuel-agnostic nahi.

Abhi problem nahi hai. India mein bikne wali zyadatar gaadiyon mein engine hai — CNG aur hybrid dono mein bhi. Demand strong hai.

Par direction ek hi taraf hai.

Capacity badhi hai — Bi-Metal 486 se 580 lakh units, Brakes 30 se 50 lakh pieces.

Jo dhyan mein rakhna hai:

EV diversification abhi early stage hai. 8-10% target hai, achieved nahi.
Auto sector cyclical hai. 36% growth strong base pe repeat karna mushkil.
Margin peak se peeche. Agle do quarter batayenge ki 24.79% high tha ya 21.92% naya normal.
Subsidiary ka sequential girna ek quarter ki baat hai ya trend, abhi saaf nahi.
Company chhoti hai. Scale, raw material aur forex ka exposure rating agency khud flag kar chuki.

Takeaway:

Har business ke apne support aur resistance hote hain — price mein nahi, numbers mein.

Menon ke liye support hai capacity, jo abhi badhi. Resistance hai margin, jo 24.79% se 21.92% pe aa gayi.

Aur ek lamba structural resistance — engine ka future.

Aaj engine hai, isliye business chal raha hai. Sawaal yeh ki jab engine kam honge, tab kya hoga.

Company ka jawab teen hisson mein hai. Alkop ke through EV components — target hai FY27 tak Alkop revenue ka 8-10% EV se aaye. Braking division, jo powertrain-neutral hai — brake har gaadi mein lagta hai. Aur Menon Bearings New Ventures, jo EV charging aur cold chain explore kar rahi hai.

Teenon abhi chhote hain. Par yehi teen track karne layak hain — inhi se pata chalega ki jawab kaam kar raha hai ya sirf plan hai.

Bottom line:

India's first GLP-1 opportunity was obvious:

Make semaglutide cheaper and sell more of it.

The next opportunity could be much deeper:

Manufacture the API, fill the injection and produce it for dozens of brands globally.

But this won't be easy money.

Peptide manufacturing is difficult.

Quality problems can delay launches, while 40+ brands can destroy pricing power quickly.

Then there’s the API opportunity.

Companies that can reliably manufacture peptide APIs can supply multiple brands instead of competing with them.

That means the GLP-1 opportunity could spread across:
API → Formulation → Fill-finish → Injector → CDMO

And we’re already seeing evidence of this.

OneSource supported a generic semaglutide programme that received tentative US FDA approval.

It has also supported approvals in Canada.

That changes the economics completely.

Imagine 40 pharma companies fighting to sell semaglutide.

The company manufacturing for 5–10 of them doesn't need to know which brand ultimately wins.

Why?
Semaglutide isn't a simple tablet.

It's a complex peptide that needs specialised manufacturing, sterile filling and reliable injector devices.

To understand where the real value could sit, break one injection into 3 layers:

Formulation - selling the medicine
API - manufacturing the peptide
CDMO - manufacturing for other pharma companies

And that creates a strange situation.

Demand for GLP-1 drugs is exploding.

But if 40+ brands are selling essentially the same molecule, competition can quickly push prices and margins down.

First, what changed?

On March 20, semaglutide's key patent expired in India.

Natco launched at just Rs.1,290/month, while companies like Sun, Dr Reddy's, Zydus, Alkem and Torrent entered the race.

Suddenly, a very expensive drug became a crowded generic market.

One of the world's biggest drugs just lost patent protection in India.

Within days, 40+ companies were ready with versions of semaglutide.

But the biggest opportunity may NOT be selling the injection.

It may be manufacturing what goes inside it. 👇

Park Medi World 

CMP: 282
MCAP: 12193 cr
P/E: 43.9

Park Medi World Limited, which runs the Park Group of Hospitals, has just set up a brand new company that it owns completely. This new company is called Park Medicity Prayagraj Limited, and it officially came into existence on September 8, 2026.

The reason they created this new entity is to build and run a large hospital in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. This will be a 550 bed multi super speciality hospital, meaning it will offer many different medical specialities under one roof.

Interestingly, this hospital project has come through a public private partnership, which means the local municipal corporation in Prayagraj has awarded this project to Park Medi World to build and operate the hospital, rather than the government building it entirely on its own.

Since Park Medi World owns one hundred percent of this new company, there is no conflict of interest here. No related parties or group companies have any special stake in this deal, and everything has been done at arm's length, meaning fairly and without favoritism.

The amount of money involved to start this new subsidiary is quite small at this stage, only about fifteen lakh rupees, used to buy one lakh fifty thousand shares in the new company. This is essentially just the initial seed capital needed to officially register the new entity. 

The bigger investment for actually building the hospital would likely come later.

This move signals that Park Medi World is expanding its footprint beyond its existing markets into a new and significant city. 

Prayagraj is a major religious and administrative hub in Uttar Pradesh, known for large events like the Kumbh Mela which draw enormous crowds, so a large modern hospital there could serve a very large population base that may currently lack access to advanced medical care.

Winning a public private partnership project is also meaningful because governments usually award such contracts only to companies they consider financially capable and credible, so it can be seen as a vote of confidence in Park Medi World's ability to execute large scale healthcare projects. 

Successfully completing this one could also make it easier for the company to win similar hospital contracts in other cities in the future, creating a template for growth through government partnerships rather than only through fully self funded new hospitals.

From a business perspective, once operational, a 550 bed hospital adds a large amount of new bed capacity to the company's overall network, which over the years should translate into a meaningful boost to revenue and profits as the hospital ramps up patient volumes. It also allows Park Medi World to diversify geographically, reducing its dependence on its current cities and giving it a foothold in a fast growing part of Uttar Pradesh.

However, since actual construction, government approvals, staffing, and eventually filling up hospital beds with patients typically take several years, the real financial benefit from this move will likely show up gradually over the coming years rather than immediately. 

In short, this is a long term growth seed being planted today, positioning the company for expanded scale and geographic reach in the healthcare sector over the next several years.

WHY HEALTHCARE CAN BE INTERESTING
The interesting part of healthcare is that revenue can be repeat in nature, depending on the business.

▪️ Hospitals → patients continuously require treatments, procedures and healthcare services.

▪️ Diagnostics → tests are performed repeatedly, creating recurring demand.

▪️ Pharma → chronic therapies and regularly prescribed medicines can provide repeat business.

▪️ Medical devices & consumables → many products are consumed or require replacement, creating repeat demand.

▪️ CDMO / contract manufacturing → once a company develops a relationship with a customer, repeat orders can potentially create long-term revenue visibility.

▪️ Healthcare platforms & services → established customer/patient networks can create recurring usage and stronger operating leverage as the business scales.

But recurring revenue doesn't automatically mean a good investment.

We still need to check the quality of the revenue, margins, cash flows, debt, working capital, customer concentration, regulatory risks, promoter quality and valuation.

Healthcare can be a very powerful compounding sector - but only when the underlying business, execution and valuation all make sense.

So don't just look at which stock has gone up.
Study the business. Track the execution. Research the numbers. Then take a decision.

Coinate Wiki #17 | PPI
Macro · Producer Inflation

PPI (Producer Price Index) measures how prices received by domestic producers change over time.

Unlike CPI, which focuses on consumer prices, PPI looks further upstream — at inflation pressures faced by businesses and producers.

Why does PPI matter?
• It tracks producer-side inflation
• It can signal future consumer price pressure
• It influences Fed rate expectations
• It can move bonds, the dollar, stocks, gold, and crypto

3 keywords to know PPI:
 Producers · Inflation · Fed

What should traders watch?
→ Headline PPI
→ Core PPI
→ Month-over-month change
→ Services and goods inflation

A hotter-than-expected PPI can suggest that cost pressures are building upstream.

A cooler reading can indicate that inflation pressure is easing before it reaches consumers.
But PPI is not a perfect predictor of CPI.

What matters is whether producer costs are becoming persistent enough to affect margins, pricing, and ultimately the broader inflation trend.

SJS Enterprises, Steel Strips Wheels and Menon Bearings show why utilisation without mix, returns and capacity sequencing is a weak KPI.

SJS: FY26 revenue grew 25.6% with a 29.6% EBITDA margin. FY27 margin guidance is 27–28%. Core chrome and paint lines are near 95% utilisation, prompting ₹260–270 Cr of three-year capex. Management expects 2.5–3x asset turns on new capacity and 4–5x in display bonding.

Sanjay Thapar: “We are increasing capacity because we see a very strong runway for growth… preparing the ground for future growth.”

“We want to grow profitably—that is the key to growth at SJS.”

Steel Strips Wheels: every unit is above 95% utilisation—something management says has not happened in 30–40 years. EBITDA per wheel rose to ₹314 from ₹282. Export revenue is targeted at ₹600 Cr, while the Bhuj knuckle expansion is committed before commissioning.

Dhiraj Garg: “All my business units are running at more than 95% utilisation.”

But on commoditised aluminium pricing: “We are not in the cash-burning business at all.”

Menon Bearings: brake EBITDA margin jumped from 12–14% to ~25% after higher-margin mix and the exit from low-margin merchant exports to Africa and Dubai. Management cautions this level may normalise; consolidated guidance is 20–21%.

Aditya Menon: “We also didn’t imagine that we could achieve that much EBITDA at brakes.”

Kyro read: SJS is adding capacity ahead of a high-return runway; SSWL is already demand-constrained; Menon improved economics by refusing bad volume. The superior signal is incremental ROCE—not utilisation alone.

Watch: asset turns, EBITDA per unit and export mix.

Risk: capacity and export ambition dilute incremental returns before mix improves.

ESDS IPO Windfall Fuels a Rare One-Day 5.19% NAV Surge for Motilal Oswal Digital India Fund

The Windfall
Motilal Oswal Digital India Fund's NAV rose 5.19% in a single day on September 4 — even as benchmark Nifty 50 gained just 0.1%

Triggered by ESDS Software's blockbuster stock market debut — stock more than doubled from its issue price

ESDS Software closed at ₹908.40 on September 4 — a gain of nearly 112% from issue price

The Anchor Allocation
Fund received anchor allocation of 10.25 lakh shares in ESDS IPO at ₹429 apiece

Total investment: ~₹44 crore

Accounted for nearly 5% of fund's assets of around ₹907 crore as of July 31, 2026

Potential Further Upside
NAV could get further boost after ESDS Software remained locked at 20% upper circuit at ₹1,090.05 on Monday

Based on fund's exposure, latest rise could translate into an additional gain of around 1% for unitholders — assuming other portfolio holdings remain unchanged

Fund Profile
AUM: ₹907 crore (as of July 31, 2026)

One-year return: 3.29%

Fund Manager: Varun Singh

Invests across broader technology ecosystem — digital, internet, AI, software and platform-led business models

Top holdings include Eternal, PB Fintech, Coforge, Hexaware Technologies, One97 Communications

Focus on "identifying well-run, scalable businesses with long-term structural growth potential" rather than any single event or listing

Context — Rarity of Such Moves
Such sharp single-day gains in equity fund NAVs are rare — schemes typically spread investments across diversified portfolio to limit impact of sharp moves in any single holding

A 6-7% upmove in a fund's NAV is usually 30-50% of a diversified equity scheme's average annual gains

Technology funds have underperformed over past year amid AI-led disruption, rotation away from momentum sectors and cooling-off in elevated valuations

BSE IT TRI has declined 13.83% in the past year while Motilal Oswal Digital India Fund has gained 3.29%

D-Street Grooves to IPO Pop, But Rally Is Highly Concentrated — 15 Stocks Drive 80% of Gains

The Headline Numbers
BSE IPO index surged 35% in first five months of FY27 — strongest April-August performance in three years

Hit an all-time high on Monday

BSE SME IPO index jumped 55% — best showing for the period in two years

Benchmark is 5% away from its record levels

How It Compares to Broader Market
Sensex and Nifty rose 6% each during April-August

BSE MidCap 150 gained 19%

BSE SmallCap 250 climbed 29%

IPO index gains far outpaced broader market

The Concentration Problem
Strong performance masks a highly concentrated rally

15 stocks account for nearly 80% of gains in BSE's 73-stock IPO index

For BSE's 105-stock SME IPO index, 24 companies contributed 34,472 points — accounting for nearly 89% of gains

Remaining 56 gainers added 6,520 points while 25 stocks dragged the index down by 22,000 points

Top Contributors to BSE IPO Index
Of 4,661 points gained between April and August, key contributors include: Meesho, Lenskart Solutions, Tata Capital, Billionbrains Garage Ventures, Rubicon Research, LG Electronics India, Physicswallah, Urban Company, Shadowfax Technologies, Sudeep Pharma, ICICI Prudential Assets, Aequs, Emmvee Photovoltaic Power, Fujiyama Power Systems and Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions — together contributing 3,738 points

How the Indices Work
A stock market debutant enters BSE IPO index on the third day after listing and is generally removed after completing one year

For SME IPO index, stock is included on the second day of listing

An SME stock exits earlier if it migrates to BSE Mainboard

Both indices rebalanced monthly

What's Driving Investor Interest
Retail and HNI investors opting for fresh growth stories over legacy large-cap names that carry FPI overhang, valuation baggage and uncertain earnings visibility

Operating margin

FADA ka August 2026 data aaya. Ek line sab jagah chal rahi hai — alternative fuels ne pehli baar petrol ko peechhe chhod diya.

Trend teen point mein:

Saal bhar pehle petrol karib 11 point aage tha.
July mein gap sirf 1 point — petrol 41.68%, alt fuels 40.59%.
August mein palat gaya — alt fuels 41.95%, petrol 40.85%.

Volume record. Total retail 24.23 lakh units, 17.51% up. PV 4.02 lakh — pehli baar August mein 4 lakh paar.

Ab 41.95% todiye:

CNG-LPG 25.28%
Hybrid 9.04%
Electric 7.63%

CNG gaadi mein engine hota hai. Hybrid mein bhi. EV mein nahi.

Matlab August mein bikne wali karib 92% gaadiyon mein abhi engine hai.

Ancillary ke liye yahi asli baat hai. EV ka nuksaan sabko barabar nahi hota.

Do tarah ke business kam exposed hain.

Pehla — jo powertrain se juda hi nahi.

Tyres — MRF, Apollo, CEAT, JK Tyre, Balkrishna.
Glass — Asahi India Glass.
Wheels aur suspension — Steel Strips Wheels, Wheels India, Gabriel.
Wiring harness — Samvardhana Motherson. EV mein content aur badhta hai.
Cables, lighting, electronics — Suprajit, Uno Minda, Fiem, Lumax.

Inka business volume se juda hai, fuel se nahi.

Doosra — jo auto ke bahar bhi kaam karte hain. Auto inke liye ek customer hai, poora business nahi.

Bharat Forge — forgings, saath mein defence, aerospace, oil-gas aur rail.
NRB Bearings — bearings, par acquisition se aerospace mein utri. AS9100D certification mil chuka. Industrial ab revenue ka 14%.
Sansera Engineering — precision components, non-auto aur aerospace-defence hissa khud badha rahi.
Dynamatic Technologies — auto hydraulics plus aerospace structures.
Sundram Fasteners — wind energy, industrial aur aerospace.
Ramkrishna Forgings — auto ke saath railway aur oil-gas.
Schaeffler India — bada industrial segment.
Timken India — bearings, railway ka hissa bada.
Craftsman Automation — machining, plus industrial engineering aur storage.
Sona BLW — EV differential gears, aur railway equipment.

Matlab yeh nahi ki yeh safe hain. Sirf itna ki inka future ek hi powertrain pe nahi tika.

Aftermarket bhi yaad rakhiye. Replacement business sadak pe khadi gaadiyon pe chalta hai, naye vehicles pe nahi. Parked fleet abhi petrol-diesel hi hai.

Ab honest side:

FADA ne khud kaha August 2025 ka base kamzor tha — log GST 2.0 rate cut ka intezaar kar rahe the. Toh 17.51% dabe base pe.
Month-on-month retail 6.48% neeche.
PV inventory 38-40 days, July se 5 din zyada. Recommended 21.
Aur diversification pe — in sab ke non-auto business abhi chhote hain, aur aerospace-defence orders ki timing predictable nahi hoti. Certification milna aur revenue aana, do alag baatein hain.

Track karne layak: EV, hybrid aur CNG ka share alag-alag — ek category mat samajhiye. Inventory days. Aur Sept-Nov ka retail.

Takeaway:

Volume sabke liye accha hai. Mix sabke liye nahi.

Aur jis company ka future ek hi industry pe nahi tika, uske paas ek option zyada hai.

I think the problem begins with the way you've framed the Catholic position.

The Catholic Church does not teach that we earn our initial justification through works, sacraments, or obedience to the Law. It teaches that justification originates entirely in God's grace and that “no one can merit the initial grace of forgiveness and justification.” So if your argument is that Paul rejects the idea that we earn our justification before God, Catholics agree with Paul.

So what did Paul mean when he wrote that we are justified “by faith apart from the deeds of the law”?

Paul's argument is that we are not justified because we have successfully kept the Law and thereby earned righteousness. We are justified by God's grace through faith in Christ. The context makes this especially clear: immediately after Romans 3:28, Paul turns to Jews and Gentiles, circumcision and uncircumcision. No one can boast that his observance of the Law has earned him righteousness before God.

But that's quite different from saying:

“Intellectual belief in Jesus is the only thing required of a Christian, and what you subsequently do is irrelevant to salvation.”

Paul never says that.

In fact, Romans itself won't allow that interpretation. Paul speaks of God rendering to each person “according to his works” and eternal life for those who persevere in doing good (Romans 2:6–7). He speaks of the “obedience of faith” at both the beginning and end of the letter (Romans 1:5; 16:26). He says faith establishes rather than abolishes the law (Romans 3:31), and later warns Christians that they can be “cut off” through unbelief (Romans 11:20–22).

And that's exactly why James 2 matters. James doesn't contradict Paul; he prevents us from turning Paul's teaching into something Paul never taught. Even the demons “believe—and shudder,” and James concludes that “faith apart from works is dead” and that a person is “justified by works and not by faith alone.”

So my qualification becomes simple: whatever “faith” means in Romans 3:28, it cannot simply mean “belief alone.”

The Bible is a seamless web. We don't get to isolate Romans 3:28 from Romans itself, much less from James, Jesus, Peter, and the rest of Scripture. Romans 3:28 and James 2:24 are both Scripture. Any theology of justification has to account honestly for both.

And that's where I think your historical conclusion goes too far. Showing that Paul taught justification by grace through faith does not demonstrate that the Church of Rome later abandoned Paul's Gospel. You first have to demonstrate that Catholic teaching actually contradicts Paul's teaching rather than a particular interpretation of Paul.

Catholicism agrees that grace comes first, that initial justification cannot be earned, and that salvation is possible only through Christ. The real disagreement is over what saving faith is and what happens after God has given us that grace.

That's a much more interesting question than simply asking whether Catholics can find the words “faith alone.”

A word is not a covenant.

“Allah” is Arabic for the god. It is a title the desert already knew, a designation any tongue can borrow. It is not the Name spoken from the fire that would not be consumed.

When Moses asked, “Who shall I say sent me?” the Voice did not answer with a common noun. He answered with Himself:

I AM WHO I AM.

Then He sealed it:
YHWH, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. This is My name forever, and this is My memorial unto all generations.
(Exodus 3:14–15)

Forever. Not until another language arrives. Not until another book claims to confirm Moses while leaving the Name He swore would never be forgotten off every page.

He said it again:
I am the LORD; that is My name. I will not give My glory to another.
(Isaiah 42:8)

A memorial spoken as eternal cannot be folded into a generic word and called the same. A glory He refuses to share cannot be absorbed by a title that never once utters YHWH.

Allah is not the Christian God.
If the Voice from the bush is the same Voice that later spoke in Arabic, why is the Name He called His own forever absent from the book that claims to stand in Moses’ line? He did not misplace it. The world did.

And then the Name returned, not as a syllable carved in stone, but as a Savior walking among us.

Jesus.
YHWH saves.

The memorial still stands.
The Name was never lost.
It was kept until it became flesh.

To insult a title is not to insult the God who named Himself. The God of the bush already told us His Name. He has not asked us to forget it.

India's households have found their lender. It is the family jewellery box.

Gold loans now make up 11.1% of all retail credit in India — up from 5.9% in 2022. In four years, pawning the family gold went from fringe credit to a double-digit share of the entire consumer lending market.

The average pledge: ₹1.96 lakh. The growth: NBFC gold loan books hit ₹3.3 lakh crore by May 2026, up 69.9% in a single year per RBI data. Origination value has multiplied fivefold since 2022.

One in five borrowers is now Gen Z — first salaries that can't cover first costs, monetizing the metal their grandmothers locked away for weddings.

The collateral base is 25,000 tonnes of household gold, and only about 6% of it is pledged. That is not a niche. That is a shadow banking system measured in bangles, waiting in the locker.

And it is almost perfectly repaid — non-performing share around 1.1%. Not because the borrowers are rich. Because the alternative to repaying is losing the family's only store of value. Lose the gold and there is no second vault. So redemption runs near-total — the collateral enforces the contract better than any court.

₹1.96 lakh against the anklets. 11.1% of retail credit against 6% of the vault. The pawn counter is now a pillar of Indian finance.

HFCL FY26 Annual Report Key Takeaways 🧵

• Strong FY26: Revenue grew 21.8% to ₹4,949 Cr, EBITDA +63.2% to ₹827 Cr and PAT +90.1% to ₹329 Cr.

• Margins expanding: EBITDA margin improved sharply to 16.7% from 12.5%, driven by better product mix and higher capacity utilisation.

• Business mix changing: Product-led revenue rose to 62% from 42%, while private customers increased to 84% from 65%.

• Exports taking off: Export contribution jumped to 41.4% from 12.2% in FY25, with >70% of cable production now serving international markets.

• Big global win: ₹10,159 Cr ($1.1B) OFC (Optical Fiber Cable) supply agreement with a global hyperscaler. Management targets exports at >50% of revenue by FY27.

• Strong visibility: Order book stood at ₹21,206 Cr in March 2026 and increased to ₹26,665 Cr by June 2026.

• Profitability is shifting: Telecom Products generated ₹2,931 Cr revenue and ₹764 Cr segment profit, while Turnkey Contracts generated ₹1,875 Cr revenue but a ₹113 Cr loss.

• Strategic pivot working: HFCL is moving from lower-margin project execution towards higher-margin, product-led businesses.

• Capacity expansion: OF capacity targeted at 38.5 mn fkm (fiber kilometer) and OFC capacity at 56.36 mn fkm by July 2028, with ~₹580 Cr being invested in backward integration into preforms.

• Defence opportunity: Defence revenue targeted at ₹500 Cr in FY27 vs ₹77 Cr in FY26, with a ~₹2,189 Cr defence/aerospace pipeline.

• Aerospace entry: Proposed acquisition brings an export-oriented ₹1,890 Cr order book, while a 1,000-acre defence facility is being developed in Andhra Pradesh.

• BharatNet optionality: HFCL has secured >₹7,335 Cr of Phase III contracts and sees upcoming opportunities worth >₹50,000 Cr.

• R&D focus: 229 R&D professionals are working across 5G, Wi-Fi, AI-enabled networking and emerging 6G technologies.

• Balance sheet: Debt increased to ₹1,713 Cr, but Net Debt/Equity remained comfortable at 0.34x.

• Key concern - cash flow: Operating cash flow was -₹335 Cr despite ₹329 Cr PAT, mainly due to higher inventory and receivables supporting the growing order book.

Overall, FY26 marks a meaningful transformation - from projects to products, domestic to global, and telecom towards a broader connectivity + defence + aerospace platform.

A couple of years ago, most investors had written this company off. Today, it is quietly staging one of the more interesting turnarounds in India's industrial space.

The company is Ramkrishna Forgings.

First, what it does.

It is one of India's largest forging companies. In simple terms, it shapes metal into the heavy, safety critical parts that vehicles and trains cannot run without, axles, crankshafts, steering knuckles, and rail wheels.

 It supplies truck makers, exports heavily to North America and Europe, and is now becoming a serious railways play.

To understand the turnaround, you have to understand what came before it.

Over the past several years, the company spent heavily, around ₹3,600 crore, building new capacity across forging, casting and machining. 

Big capex like this always hurts before it helps. Debt piled up to nearly ₹2,400 crore, profits shrank, and to make matters worse, its biggest export market, US heavy trucks, went into a slump. Add several years of missed guidance, and the market simply lost patience.

But that is exactly the point most people miss. The hard part, the spending, is now done. And the capacity it built is finally starting to pay off.

Here is the cycle now playing out.

The capacity is in place. The order book is strong and getting executed. That is driving revenue growth. And as the plants run fuller, operating leverage kicks in, the same fixed costs spread over more output, so margins expand. 

In the latest quarter, profit jumped more than 3x from a year ago, and gross margin rose from about 49% to around 54%, helped by a shift toward higher value parts.

The best part of the cycle is what happens next. This is now throwing off strong cash flow, its operating cash flow last year was the highest in company history, and that cash is going straight into cutting debt.

From a peak of about ₹2,400 crore, net debt has already fallen by more than ₹500 crore in three quarters, with more reduction guided. 

Lower debt means lower interest, which means even more profit. A virtuous loop.

Now, the biggest growth engine: railways.

Through a joint venture, the company is commissioning one of Asia's largest forged rail wheel plants, and it is weeks away from bulk supply to Indian Railways. 

But this turnaround is far from guaranteed.

Energy and freight costs are still squeezing margins. Debt, while falling, is still meaningful. And this is a management that has missed its own targets for several years, so credibility is on the line. 

Execution over the next few quarters is everything, and there are governance points worth watching too.

The bigger picture, though, is hard to ignore.

If the execution holds, the company that emerges looks very different from the one investors gave up on.

That is what makes this one worth watching closely.

My important pointers from the Annual Report of Quality Power Systems :

QPOWER is trying to evolve from a specialised reactor/coil manufacturer into a broader grid-technology platform spanning HVDC + FACTS + power electronics + BESS PCS + GIS components + transformer components + digital substations.

QPOWER is trying to position itself as a single-shop / integrated solution provider for high-voltage grid infrastructure and power-quality systems, rather than just a reactor or coil manufacturer.

It has various subsidiaries for different products, and each product provides synergies with other products under the same group.

HVDC & FACTS — reactors, harmonic filters, STATCOM/SVC-related equipment and 800 kV-class products.- Quality power 

Instrument transformers — through Mehru, including high-voltage CT/PT and emerging GIS-related capability

GIS (gas-insulated substations) components — being developed with Hyosung as the next technology pillar.

Transformer components — tanks, fabrication and assemblies through Sukrut.

BESS grid interface — PCS + transformers + instrument transformers + reactors + harmonic filters can potentially be supplied together from within the group.-- Advantage from synergies.

Digital substations/grid automation — SCADA-DMS, RTUs, cybersecurity, IoT and edge computing through Inavitas Endoks and Nebeskie.

Potential insulator capability — via the proposed Winwin Speciality Insulators acquisition.

It has now undertaken a major capacity expansion at its Sangli facility that practically increases its capacity by 9x and will be commercialised from Q2 FY27.
A 320000 sq ft facility.

The changes are very material for a compay trying to lead in the HVDC and FACTS market and trying to compete with global mnc's like Hitachi Energy etc.

The management has a clear ambition to become the next hitachi energy originating from India.

I knew little about the corporate fundamentals other than they were the fastest growing coffee house retailer in North America, with the largest consumer economy in the world aiding its expansion. That was 26+ years ago! Starbucks wasn’t the sexiest girl at the dance 💃 but she brought me to self-directed investing, so I stuck with the girl who brought me to the dance.

And just like, almost exactly like the former Dotcom boom, the AI boom is growing from the enterprise toward the future consumer market. But that future can take upwards of a decade before scaling and has NEVER scaled profitably ie $AMZN 

The difference, and this is likely to be the only difference when the saga is said and done ✅, is that the post Dotcom boom monopoly business models have a pre-existing and dominant revenue stream entering the AI boom 💥, which should be sustained post the AI build out phase. 

What’s not different today, are the investor capital returns from the coinciding earnings boom 🤯. Having said that, and recognizing today that there remains no mass consumer service/product ideas for AI akin to no scaled Dotcom 2000 conssumer service/product, the outcome post the AI buildout phase likely has a similar outcome to 2000, that most willingly CHOOSE to assuage and/or egotistical ignore for the sake of… the moment.

PB Fintech beyond Q1 FY27 numbers 

PB Fintech’s next phase looks broader than just selling more insurance.

Health and term remain the core opportunity. New health and term premium grew 53% YoY, while 82% of customers coming to PB are new to insurance. Monthly payment options are also helping make health insurance more affordable.

Renewals could become the next earnings driver. Renewal revenue is already growing 55%, and management expects 50% growth for some time as customers acquired over the last few years start renewing.

PB Partners is expanding the opportunity offline and into smaller cities. It has 5 lakh advisors, while 78% of its premium already comes from tier 2 and 3 cities.

Paisabazaar has reached operating breakeven and is expanding beyond loans into daily SIPs, bonds, payments and PB Money. According to management, these are initially meant to increase customer engagement rather than profits.

PB Health is the biggest new bet. Two hospitals are now operational, with management targeting around ₹500 Cr annual revenue run rate and breakeven by March 2027. If it works, PB gets exposure to both health insurance and healthcare delivery.

AI is another potential lever. It already touches 30% to 40% of PB’s 10 crore monthly customer interactions and could improve sales conversion, servicing and productivity.

The key point is that management still prefers "growth over margins". Rising renewals and AI can improve profitability, but much of the benefit will be reinvested for customer growth.

The opportunity is large across insurance penetration, renewals, offline distribution and healthcare. The risks are equally clear; regulatory changes, continued high customer acquisition spending, execution in hospitals and maintaining focus across many new businesses.

QPOWER has the ingredients to become a much larger company by FY28–30.
But future earnings, not P/E expansion, must drive the next leg of returns.
18/
The key question isn't:
"Is Quality Power a good company?"
I think it is.
The real question is:
Can ₹1,945 Cr of orders + 9× capacity + Mehru + BESS + GIS translate into ₹280–300 Cr+ PAT by FY28?
If yes, today's valuation can make sense.
If not, the stock is expensive.
19/
My takeaway:
Great business + huge structural opportunity + strong order visibility — but high expectations are already embedded in the price.
For me, the next few quarters are about execution, not storytelling.
That is the QPOWER thesis.

🧵 Quality Power Electrical Equipments — Future Growth & Valuation
1/
Quality Power is becoming much more than a conventional electrical-equipment company.
Its opportunity spans:
⚡ HVDC
⚡ FACTS
⚡ Reactors
⚡ Power Electronics
⚡ GIS
⚡ BESS/PCS
⚡ Instrument Transformers
⚡ Transformer Components
The interesting part is what comes next. 🧵
2/
FY26 was transformational:
Revenue: ₹1,007 Cr
EBITDA: ₹236 Cr
PAT: ₹186 Cr
PAT attributable: ~₹121 Cr
EPS: ₹15.67
But FY26's 157% revenue growth shouldn't simply be extrapolated because acquisitions, especially Mehru, changed the consolidated base.
3/
The real indicator is the order book.
FY26-end: ₹1,400+ Cr
By Q1 FY27: ~₹1,945 Cr
That's almost 2× FY26 revenue.
More importantly, the mix is moving toward HVDC, FACTS, power electronics and high-value engineered products.
4/
Why is the opportunity so large?
Renewables + grid modernisation + HVDC + electrification + AI/data centres + energy storage are driving massive investment in electricity infrastructure.
Quality Power sits directly in several of these value chains.
5/
The biggest bet is Sangli.
The new Global Coil Manufacturing facility is expected to increase coil-production capacity by nearly 9×.
It's designed for large-scale HVDC, FACTS and reactor/coil demand.
This could materially change the company's revenue capacity.
6/
Other capacity additions:
• HVDC CTC Magnet Wire facility
• Mehru GIS/high-voltage testing
• Endoks PCS/BESS facility
• Sukrut transformer components
So the company isn't simply waiting for the existing business to grow.
It's building capacity ahead of demand.
7/
Mehru
Quality Power owns 51%.
FY26:
Revenue: ~₹316 Cr
PBT: ~₹40 Cr
PAT: ~₹30 Cr
Order book: >₹350 Cr
The acquisition appears to be turning into a meaningful growth engine rather than merely adding revenue.
8/
BESS could be a major optionality.
Endoks already has expertise in STATCOM, SVC, harmonic filters and power converters.
Now it is entering PCS for Battery Energy Storage Systems.
India's storage requirement could reach ~236 GWh by FY32.
Still early, but potentially enormous.
9/
The exciting part is cross-selling.
A BESS project could potentially require:
Endoks → PCS
Quality Power → Reactors/filters
Mehru → Instrument Transformers
Sukrut → Transformer components
This creates the possibility of capturing multiple parts of the same project ecosystem.
10/
My base-case estimates
FY27:
Revenue: ₹1,208 Cr
PAT: ₹169 Cr
EPS: ~₹21.8
FY28:
Revenue: ₹1,812 Cr
EBITDA: ₹399 Cr
PAT: ~₹290 Cr
EPS: ~₹37.4
These are my estimates, NOT company guidance.
11/
FY29, assuming growth normalises:
Revenue: ~₹2,265 Cr
EBITDA: ~₹498 Cr
PAT: ~₹374 Cr
EPS: ~₹48
This is where the long-term thesis becomes interesting.
But execution is everything.
12/
At ~₹1,495/share and ~₹11,600 Cr market cap:
FY27 P/E → ~68×
FY28 P/E → ~40×
FY29 P/E → ~31×
So QPOWER is not cheap today.
The market is already pricing significant FY28 success.
13/
FY28 valuation scenarios:
🔴 Bear: EPS ~₹22.6 → 66× P/E
🟡 Base: EPS ~₹37.4 → 40× P/E
🟢 Bull: EPS ~₹45.3 → 33× P/E
The current valuation requires the growth story to actually materialise.
14/
Using a 40–55× FY28 P/E:
EPS ₹37.4 gives:
40× → ₹1,498
45× → ₹1,683
50× → ₹1,870
55× → ₹2,057
So at ₹1,495, the stock is roughly pricing a successful FY28 base case.
15/
The biggest risks:
❌ 9× capacity expansion execution
❌ Working-capital requirements
❌ Acquisition/integration risk
❌ Copper/CRGO/raw-material volatility
❌ Potential dilution from future fundraising
❌ High starting valuation
A great business can still produce poor returns if bought too expensively.
16/
The 5 things I want to watch over the next 4–6 quarters:
Sangli commissioning
Order-book conversion
Revenue acceleration
EBITDA margin staying ≥20%
PAT converting into cash
If these happen, the valuation becomes much easier to justify.
17/
Final view
Business: 🟢 8.5/10
Industry: 🟢 9/10
Growth potential: 🟢 9/10
Balance sheet: 🟢 Strong

The Indian IT sector is having an identity crisis.

Nifty IT is down ~17% YTD. TCS and Wipro are down 26–30%.
Coforge? Up. Persistent? Quietly holding ground.

Same sector. Completely different story.

Here's what's actually happening:

US clients are deploying AI agents.
One agent replaces 10 deployed analysts.
Headcount-per-deal drops.
Revenue-per-employee drops.
TCV goes up (deals look big on paper).
But actual revenue doesn't follow.
EPS growth slows. P/E de-rates.

That's the chain. And large caps are stuck in it.

Mid-caps like Coforge cracked the code differently:
Smaller teams. Faster deployment. Outcome-based pricing.
AI augments delivery instead of deflating it.

The 4 metrics that'll separate winners in Q2 FY27:
→ % of revenue explicitly tagged as AI revenue
→ Agent-per-FTE ratio (are they replacing or augmenting?)
→ GenAI margin impact disclosed (accretive or dilutive?)
→ Deal structure shift — FTE-based vs outcome-based %

TCV is a lagging indicator now.
Revenue realization is the only number that matters.

The irony? Bigger the firm, bigger the deflation surface.

Q2 results start October. September is your preview window.

#QuestioningConvictionMuscle | Week ended 4 Sep 2026

The S&P 500 edged higher while Nifty fell for a fourth week.

Fear rose, yet volatility stayed subdued. Is this stress, rotation, or denial?

Market Pulse
S&P 500: +0.1%, closing 7,718.60.
Nifty 50: -1.2%, closing 23,897.70.

CNN Fear & Greed fell from 52, Neutral, to 42, Fear.
India's MMI fell from 49.46 to 43.87, both Fear.

US VIX ended at 14.53, up 0.10 point.
India VIX ended at 10.68, unchanged for the week despite a 5.8% Friday fall.

US and India Sector Divergence

US energy led as crude rose roughly 10%. Technology ranked next, but hardware strength hid a software selloff. Utilities also advanced. Equal-weight S&P 500 fell 0.8% while the NYSE 100 gained 0.7%, exposing narrow leadership beneath the flat headline index.

India was broader risk-off: 12 of 16 major sectors fell. Autos lost 4%, midcaps fell 1.5%, while smallcaps gained 0.1%. Coal India rose 3.6% on better earnings visibility. Capital-market stocks bounced Friday after SEBI said it would review derivatives settlement pricing. Price says selective rotation, sentiment says fear.

Announcements That Matter
• TCS, weekend: HyperVault secured 264 acres for a phased Hyderabad AI data-centre campus up to 1GW. TCS and partners expect investment up to ₹70,000 crore. The project is not operating. Watch customers, power and commissioning.

• Broadcom: Q3 revenue rose 86% to $29.6 billion. AI semiconductor revenue reached $16.7 billion, up 221%, while free cash flow was $13.7 billion. Q4 guidance is $34.8 billion. Watch whether growth holds without weaker margins.

• Nvidia: Agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93 billion. Nvidia says the platform will remain open, multi-cloud and multi-accelerator. The strategic prize is developer distribution. Watch regulatory review and whether non-Nvidia hardware retains equal access.

• Sun Pharma: Joined nine manufacturers in US most-favoured-nation pricing agreements covering state Medicaid and future innovative medicines. The group committed at least $19.6 billion to US manufacturing. Watch company-specific pricing, capex and margin disclosure before assigning winners or losers.

• ICICI Bank and LIC, weekend: RBI approved LIC to lift its aggregate ICICI Bank holding to 9.99% of paid-up capital or voting rights within one year. Permission, not purchase. Watch shareholding disclosures.

• Adobe: Anil Chakravarthy will become CEO on 1 Dec; Shantanu Narayen moves to executive chair. With earnings due 10 Sep, the test is whether leadership change sharpens Adobe's AI monetisation story.

• Lululemon: Q2 revenue fell 4% and comparable sales fell 9%. Management guided Q3 revenue down 10% to 11% and FY2026 revenue down 5% to 7%. Watch Americas demand, markdowns and tariff-adjusted margins.

Small Company, Big Signal

E2E Networks signed a binding term sheet worth about ₹1,000 crore for Nvidia Blackwell cloud GPUs and services through June 2029, roughly four times FY2026 revenue. 

A term sheet is not recognised revenue. Billing milestones, customer concentration, utilisation and depreciation will decide the economics.

Cross-Border Government Signals

Global Signal, India Implication: BLS reported 162,000 US payroll additions in August. Resilient labour demand keeps US rate risk alive, raising the hurdle for Indian valuations and foreign flows.

India Signal, Global Implication: MoSPI reported Q1 goods-and-services exports up 25.8%, imports up 30.5% and machinery imports up 51.5%.

India is exporting faster while importing capital goods even faster, supporting global suppliers but increasing exposure to oil, currencies and financing costs.

Policy Winners & Losers

Potential winners include domestic data-centre suppliers and US manufacturing beneficiaries. 

Potential losers include pharma products exposed to lower public-program pricing. 

SEBI's settlement-price review may help market platforms, but final rules will determine the economics.

Consumer Temperature, Measured

RBI's July surveys covered 5,987 urban and 8,581 rural respondents. Current Situation indices fell to 88.3 from 90.7 in cities and 91.7 from 95.2 in rural areas. Yet non-essential-spending net responses improved to 3.3 from -0.8 urban and 32.4 from 30.1 rural. Households felt worse about conditions while reporting more discretionary spending.

Where Capital Is Crowding

US concentration is visible: equal-weight S&P 500 fell 0.8% while the NYSE 100 gained 0.7%, and hardware beat software. 

India's clearest crowding evidence remains primary markets: average IPO subscriptions rose to 59.1 times from 24.5 times, while listing gains climbed to 19.5% from 5.7%. 

AI announcements show capital clustering, but announcements alone do not prove a crowded trade. Watch breadth, pricing discipline and capex returns.

Greed & Pain

Greed sits in primary-market demand and the expanding AI-capex narrative, where announcements can be priced before utilisation and returns appear.

Pain sits in Indian autos, US consumer discretionary, software weakness and higher yields. The disagreement: fear gauges worsened, yet both volatility indices stayed low.

Failed Expectations

India's 7.8% real GDP growth did not lift Nifty. Strong US payrolls of 162,000 were good economic news, yet yields rose and the S&P 500 fell Friday. Good data did not mean easy money.

Week Ahead, 7 to 13 Sep

• 7 Sep: US markets closed for Labor Day.
• 10 Sep: US August PPI at 8:30 am ET. ECB decision at 14:15 CET, press conference at 14:45 and projections at 15:45. Oracle and Adobe report after the US close.
• 11 Sep: US August CPI at 8:30 am ET.

Inflation and the ECB will test the rate narrative. Oracle and Adobe will test whether AI spending is producing revenue beyond semiconductors.

Strongest Counterargument

The bearish read may be too neat. S&P 500, Nasdaq, Russell 2000 and Indian smallcaps gained while volatility stayed low. This may be rotation under pressure. Broader participation, easing yields and stable guidance would support that view. Rising volatility alongside weaker breadth and earnings cuts would refute it.

Conviction Check

• Is oil now the binding constraint for India's earnings and inflation?
• Can AI infrastructure earn returns before hardware depreciates?
• Does US software weakness challenge the AI monetisation story?
• Are IPO buyers pricing growth, scarcity, or exit liquidity?

One Rabbit Hole
Track who captures each ₹100 of AI spending: chips, networking, power, cooling, cloud operators, or software. That may matter more than capex headlines.

Which assumption in this week's market story would you challenge first?

We screened Q1 FY27 (April to June 2026) results for midcap CDMO names with 50%+ company-wide revenue growth.

Short answer: the list is thin. Most CRDMO players run mixed books (API plus formulations plus contract manufacturing), project timing is lumpy, and several of the cleanest names have already moved into largecap territory.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗰𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗻 𝗵𝗶𝘁

𝗡𝗲𝘂𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗟𝗮𝗯𝗼𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘀 (market cap around ₹25,000 crore)
Revenue up around 116 to 119% YoY to around ₹641 to 650 crore. Commercial CMS/CDMO projects did the heavy lifting, with export traction across Europe and the US. Margins expanded sharply alongside.

𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗴, 𝗯𝘂𝘁 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝟱𝟬%

𝗦𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗽𝗮 𝗠𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗿𝗲 (around ₹18,800 crore): revenue up 43 to 45%. Formulations more than doubled, specialty CDMO picking up.

𝗔𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗶 𝗣𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗯𝘀 (around ₹7,800 crore): revenue up 39 to 42%, with fresh capex announced for additional capacity.

𝗜𝗻𝗻𝗼𝘃𝗮 𝗖𝗮𝗽𝘁𝗮𝗯 (around ₹6,700 crore): revenue up 34%. CDMO segment, at around 70% of the book, grew around 32%.

𝗔𝗸𝘂𝗺𝘀 𝗗𝗿𝘂𝗴𝘀 (around ₹12,000 crore): topline up 14%, core CDMO revenue up 18 to 19%.

𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗱 𝗕𝗶𝗼𝘁𝗲𝗰𝗵 (around ₹16,400 crore): up 26%. API led, with CDMO ambitions.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗶𝘇𝗲 𝗳𝗶𝗹𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝘀 𝗱𝗼𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲

Laurus Labs reported CDMO revenue up around 67%, and Divi's CDMO grew around 50%. Both sit outside the midcap bucket, so they fall out of this screen even though the underlying trend is identical.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱

The structural story is intact: China plus one, more commercial stage work shifting to India, peptides, ADCs, complex chemistry.

But one quarter tells you very little in this business. Shipment timing and the development versus commercial mix can swing a quarter hard in either direction. What matters is order book conversion, client concentration and utilisation tracked across four to six quarters, not a single YoY print.

Gold financing stocks have had a strong year. IIFL up 50%, Manappuram 19%, FedFina 18%, Muthoot 3%, CSB down 8%.

Three things went right at once. Gold ran to records through FY26, which meant a lender could advance more against the same jewellery without changing anything about how it operated. Unsecured credit tightened after the microfinance mess, pushing borrowers toward the one asset most Indian households already own. And the RBI's new framework, which the market had braced for, landed friendlier than feared: more headroom on small consumption loans, no cap at all on income-generation loans, and no prior approval needed to open branches. That last one is why every lender in the group is suddenly expanding.

The first of those has now reversed. Domestic gold fell roughly 15% between the end of January and the end of June. That matters more in this sector than in most, because a gold loan book is short. It rolls inside a year, so it reflects current prices rather than prices from a long time ago. While the metal was rising, growth arrived without anyone having to do much. Now it has to come from grams pledged, and tonnage grows in single digits a quarter, not in the forties.

This is why FY27 guidance sits so far below what FY26 delivered. Muthoot grew 49% last year and is guiding 15% for this one.

The structural case is intact. Most gold lending in India still happens outside the formal system, with pawnbrokers and jewellers, and that share moves to organised lenders every year. Branch expansion is easier than it has been in over a decade. Demand from rural and semi-urban borrowers is steady and not especially rate-sensitive.

So the sector probably keeps growing. It just stops growing the easy way. FY26 was a year when the collateral did the work. FY27 is a year when the lender has to.

Coal India Output and Dispatch Set to Accelerate as Monsoon Effect Wanes

✅As the intense rains over coal command regions show clear signs of easing, coal production and supplies at Coal India Limited (CIL) are gathering pace and are set to improve further from here on. Despite prolonged spells of rain through July and August, particularly across the East-Central parts, CIL maintained a steady supply run. 

✅During April–August of the current fiscal, CIL supplied 322.90 million Tonnes (MT) of coal, 6.70% higher than the 302.60 MT supplied during the corresponding period last year.

✅The easing rainfall is already bringing relief on the ground. Coal beds that had turned sticky and wet after prolonged rain exposure are now drying out, making freshly mined coal free-flowing and considerably easier to transfer, handle and dispatch through Coal Handling Plants (CHPs). 

✅Coal seams at lower mine horizons that had been submerged are being restored to production through augmented pumping, while repair of internal haul roads is progressing in full swing.

✅Mines across CIL are consequently stepping up preparations to return to full operational pace, with the focus firmly on ensuring that production and coal movement pick up quickly as ground conditions continue to improve. 

✅While average daily coal production during the rain-affected first three days of September stood at around 1.36 MT per day, it rose to approximately 1.7 MT per day  on 04.09.2026, even with just a single day's respite from rain.

PB Fintech’s healthcare strategy is becoming much more than just selling health insurance.

The company incorporated PB Healthcare Services Pvt Ltd in January 2025 and invested about ₹539.4 crore during FY26. After external investors also put in capital, PB Fintech’s stake diluted to 28.46%, making PB Healthcare an associate rather than a subsidiary.

PB Healthcare now sits above multiple healthcare-related entities, including:

Karan Apartments & Complexes

All are classified as healthcare-related businesses in PB Fintech’s FY26 accounts.

THE CAPITAL COMMITMENT IS ALREADY MEANINGFUL

At March 2026, PB Healthcare reported:

Current assets: ₹1,479.8 crore
Non-current assets: ₹788.6 crore
Equity: ₹1,895.2 crore

FY26 operating revenue was still only around ₹42.9 crore, alongside ₹80.2 crore of other income, while the business reported a small loss of around ₹1.5 crore.

So this is clearly an early-stage business with substantial capital already sitting inside the healthcare vehicle.

WHY COULD THIS MAKE STRATEGIC SENSE?

Policybazaar already sits at the intersection of customers, insurers and hospitals. PB Care+ is designed to coordinate admission, documentation, cashless approvals and discharge, while extending engagement into tele-consultation, preventive care and OPD services. 

That potentially gives PB Fintech something traditional hospital chains do not have: Insurance distribution + claims data + customer relationships + healthcare access.

THE BIG DRAMA: CRUDE OIL NEAR $96

Brent crude surged near $96 during the week because of West Asia tensions. India imports most of its oil. Higher crude means higher inflation and a bigger import bill. The market hates that.

Things calmed down by Friday after some diplomatic moves but the risk is still there. Any escalation next week and crude will spike again.

- US Fed: Governor Christopher Waller signaled support for keeping rates unchanged. That gave markets some relief on Friday.
- US Jobs Data: Came in softer than expected. This boosted risk appetite and helped the Friday bounce.
- US 30-year bond yield stayed elevated at 5.25%. Global investors remain scared of US rates.

- DII Buying: Domestic institutions bought Rs 23,156 crore this week. They basically saved us from a much bigger crash.

The Tug-of-War: When US bond yields rise, FIIs sell. When DIIs buy, they balance it out. This fight continues every single day.

Rupee Strengthened: The rupee gained 89 paise to Rs 94.49 per dollar. This is a two month high. The RBI's FCNR scheme mobilized over 127 billion dollars in NRI inflows.

In most categories where your product can be copied or incrementally improved by a peer, the eventual winner is the one that cracks distribution, not necessarily the one with the best product.

This is why we've seen such disproportionate value creation in distribution-led businesses: Zomato, PB Fintech, Blinkit, Paytm.

Now compare that with physical product or brand businesses. There are great brands, but the list of truly massive outcomes is much shorter. More importantly, brands are rarely winner-take-all. Consumers happily buy multiple brands, switch between them, and the next brand is always one scroll away.

The internet changed the equation. E-commerce, quick commerce, and digital marketplaces have made distribution instant, blanket, and algorithmic. Products can reach millions of customers overnight—but so can competitors.

The platform increasingly decides what the customer sees first. Whoever pays more, ranks higher, or gets better placement gets the click. In many ways, distribution is making part of the choice for the customer.

That makes brands less able to capture value. Products get copied faster, customer acquisition is controlled by the distribution layer, and differentiation erodes much more quickly than it did in the offline world.

The irony is that the same forces that made it possible for Sugar—and hundreds of other digital-first brands—to emerge are now making it much harder for them to survive.

India's power infrastructure boom is creating another manufacturing cycle underneath it.

CG Power has rolled out the first transformer from its new greenfield facility at Sehore, Madhya Pradesh — a ₹792 crore investment designed to become India's largest single-location power transformer manufacturing facility.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗲

🏭 50-acre manufacturing campus

⚡ 45,000 MVA planned annual capacity

🔌 220 kV to 1,200 kV transformers

🏗️ Up to 35 power transformers per month

👥 2,000+ direct and indirect jobs expected

🌍 Domestic + export markets

The plant has begun operations with an initial installed capacity of 10,000 MVA, with the remaining capacity to be commissioned progressively.

At full scale, CG Power's combined transformer manufacturing capacity across its facilities is expected to reach 1,20,000 MVA annually.

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗜𝘁 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀

Look at what's driving demand.

Renewable energy.

Transmission expansion.

Data centres.

Railways.

Industrial infrastructure.

Exports.

Every gigawatt of new generation and every major new power-consuming facility eventually creates demand for the infrastructure that moves and manages electricity.

𝗠𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗣𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿 → 𝗠𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗚𝗿𝗶𝗱𝘀 → 𝗠𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗲𝗿𝘀 → 𝗠𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗘𝗹𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗘𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗽𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁

And CG Power's existing transformer plants are already operating at full capacity.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗕𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗦𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆

India's infrastructure investment cycle isn't creating opportunities only for power generators or EPC companies.

It's creating a parallel manufacturing opportunity for the companies supplying the equipment underneath those projects.

Transformers. Switchgear. Cables. Grid equipment. Storage systems.

As India builds more renewable capacity, transmission networks and AI data centres, electrical equipment could become one of the less visible — but critical — beneficiaries.

𝗜𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗮 𝗶𝘀𝗻'𝘁 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝗻𝗳𝗿𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲.

𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝗮𝗹𝘀𝗼 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗹𝘆 𝗶𝘁.

High dividend yield shares: What happened to them over 10 years? 

Castrol: 237 to 185
Coal India: 324 to 401
Balmer Lawrie: 115 to 173
Infosys: 518 to 1144
ITC: 244 to 427 (incl hotels)

Just some random examples. Add 4-5% dividend

One of the most interesting cases to see is Hind Zinc. Look at the balance sheet transformation when they paid high dividends to fund Vedanta. Huge net cash to almost none in 3yrs

Instead of just checking dividend yield, it's better to also check underlying business growth and sustainability. Multiple compression is a huge risk here as seen with Castrol/ITC/Infy and so is cyclical/flat growth (Coal India)

Imho buying a growth co which steadily increases dividends might work better by year 5 or 10 because both might end up paying the same on cost basis. To each his own though. If done right, this style can get 9-10% returns, but the risk? Full year's dividend can be wiped out on 1 bad day

FDI is not low. Net FDI is low because many private equity investors have cashed in their stake holding in the stock market and taken out the money. Investors in Eternal, Swiggy, payTM, etc have made handsome money. MNC owners of LG, Whirlpool etc have made money in the stock market.

Many Indian companies are investing outside India diversifying into various markets. That's creation of Indian MNCs.

Then ofcourse, FIi outflows have been strong.

Net net, while inward FDI is close to 100B $, outward FDI+repatriation of equity cashout have been strong.

Why? Because 2 or 3 major reasons...

1. Domestic stock market valuations are higher than international markets. Even now inspite of 2 year flat broader market, our stocks are richly valued. This is a pervert incentive for equity holders to sell .

2. Investors in Startups like Eternal, PB Fintech and various other privately held companies got an exit for their investments. Isn't this something to be celebrated? You invest in the startups to cash out later. And you are doing in the Indian market which means private equity investors have now more reason to invest in newer startups. This signals to the international investors that indian startup companies are investible.

3. FII outflows have been due to multiple reasons and one of them is AI story. We are neither in hardware nor software. AI is  a major disruptor. Even in US it's the top software/tech companies where in estor money has flowed and not into other old world companies. 

While the first 2 reasons above are due to success of indian economy the last one isba structural weakness. 

To conclude, while the economy can grow quote well the stock markets may not perform always.

🚨 NSE IPO: THE IPO THAT COULD UNLOCK VALUE ACROSS THE MARKET! 🚨

SEBI has cleared the way for the much-awaited NSE IPO, potentially making it one of India’s biggest-ever IPOs. The proposed issue is expected to be around ₹30,000 Cr, with ~14.89 Cr shares (~6%) offered through an OFS. 

But here's the interesting part 👇

💰 NSE itself won't receive fresh capital.
Existing shareholders will monetize their holdings.

🔥 Potential direct beneficiaries:
• SBI — ~2.48 Cr shares
• Bank of Baroda — ~1.10 Cr

Eugen von Böhm-Bawerk did more damage to socialist economics than any government commission ever managed. Working in Vienna in the 1880s and 1890s, he dismantled the labor theory of value with surgical precision, showing that capital goods derive their worth from future consumer goods, not from the hours workers spent producing them.

His capital theory was the real achievement. Time matters in production. A fisherman with a net catches more fish than one with bare hands because someone sacrificed present consumption to build the tool. Interest is the price of time itself; it compensates the saver for waiting. Governments that suppress interest rates through central banking don't abolish this premium. They hide it, distorting the entire structure of production until the inevitable crash forces you to pay the bill anyway.

Böhm-Bawerk also destroyed Karl Marx personally, publishing his 1896 critique "Karl Marx and the Close of His System" with the quiet confidence of a man who had already won. Marx's three volumes of Capital contained internal contradictions Böhm-Bawerk traced systematically, brick by brick.

He served as Austrian Finance Minister three separate times and resigned each time over deficit spending. Intellectual integrity from a government official: rare then and rarer now.

India is scrambling to rebuild coal stocks at power plants.

The government has asked captive mines and key Coal India subsidiaries to increase coal loading as inventories at some power plants tighten.

Coal India’s supplies rose 6.7% YoY to 322.9 million tonnes in the first five months of FY27.

But power demand has been growing even faster.

Electricity consumption has stayed above 10% growth since May, driven by cooling, irrigation and economic activity.

As a result, coal stocks at thermal power plants have fallen to around 28.6 million tonnes — from 59.3 million tonnes at the start of FY27.

Why does this matter?

India is producing more coal, but rising power demand is eating into the fuel buffer at power plants.

That makes reliable coal supply increasingly important for the thermal power sector, while higher loading and dispatch could support the coal mining and rail freight sectors.
